records.topology: Release feature overview grouped by domain (Internationalization, Accessibility, Camera and media, Developer productivity, User experience, Graphics): per-app language preferences with auto-generated localeConfig from resources, dynamic locale updates for A/B experiments and regional customization, IME language matching, the Grammatical Inflection API justified by user harm (3 billion people speak gendered languages; wrong-gender addressing negatively impacts performance and attitude), and regional preferences (temperature units, first day of week, numbering systems).
records.traversal: Domain sections to API guides; API diff report and behavior-changes docs linked for impact analysis.
records.responsiveBehavior: Sections stack; version picker in the releases nav.
records.visualWorld: Release documentation where an API justification cites human impact (misgendered address harms performance and attitude), not just capability.
strengths: The Grammatical Inflection API is justified with the human cost of getting it wrong
Per-app language tooling automates the localeConfig from project resources, removing manual file maintenance
Dynamic locale updates enable regional A/B experiments without app releases
weaknesses: Feature density per page makes single-feature deep links necessary
Version pages age into archive status without a visible banner here
transferableDecisions: Justify i18n APIs with the human cost of getting language wrong
Automate locale configuration generation from existing resources

records.title: Android Data Backup Overview
records.firstScreenJob: Define the three data categories to preserve (identity, app data, settings) and the restore semantics per category.
records.topology: Developer guide: the data triad with per-category mechanisms (identity via Block Store credential transfer and Google sign-in, app data via sync adapters, settings restorable even without sign-in), a permissions note (granted permissions auto-backup on API 24+, but uninstall clears them), a settings checklist including transparent flags (has-seen-setup-wizard booleans), and an instability warning against backing up URIs with the ringtone example (restored URI may point to nothing on the new device).
records.traversal: Concept sections to mechanism docs (Block Store, sync adapters, key-value backup).
records.responsiveBehavior: Figures stack; note boxes highlight version semantics.
records.visualWorld: Data-continuity documentation where emotional stakes (users discovering something missing on a new phone) justify the engineering checklist.
strengths: The data triad scopes backup work to three named categories
The URI instability warning includes a concrete failure story (ringtone preference)
Transparent settings (seen-wizard flags) are explicitly included in backup scope
weaknesses: Multiple backup mechanisms (Block Store, sync adapters, auto backup) lack a decision table
Quota and file-size guidance lives in linked pages
transferableDecisions: Scope backup guidance to named data categories with per-category mechanisms
Document restore-instability cases with concrete user-facing failure stories

records.title: Android Enterprise Work Profile
records.firstScreenJob: Explain the work profile as separation of work and personal data, with privacy boundaries and deletion rules.
records.topology: Support article: the separation model (organization manages work apps and data; personal apps, data, and usage remain private), a privacy note (work apps cannot access personal SMS on Android 11+), discovery (work tab in Passwords and accounts, searchable in Android 14+), the briefcase icon convention and gray icons when paused, pause and resume flows, and deletion rules (personal ownership or relinquished company ownership required, Device Policy app must be uninstalled, all profile data deleted).
records.traversal: Question-based H2s (Does my device have, How do I access, How do I delete); related articles chain to privacy specifics.
records.responsiveBehavior: Single-column article; help-community escalation in footer.
records.visualWorld: Enterprise documentation written for the employee, where organizational control and personal privacy are both stated as guarantees.
strengths: The privacy boundary is stated as a two-way guarantee (org manages work data, personal usage stays private)
Deletion rules name the ownership precondition and the exact artifact (Device Policy app)
The briefcase icon convention gives users a visual detection method
weaknesses: Version-dependent behaviors (Android 9, 11, 14) scatter across the article
No screenshot of the work tab for visual confirmation
transferableDecisions: State enterprise privacy boundaries as two-way guarantees
Give users a visual convention (icon badge) to detect managed apps

records.responsiveBehavior: Concept table scrolls; code tabs per DSL.

weaknesses: No performance or comfort guidance (frame rates, motion) at this level

transferableDecisions: Compress new interaction paradigms into a few named primitives

records.topology: Getting-started guide: how passes work (time and location enabled, push-updatable, NFC or barcode redemption), the five styles (boarding pass, coupon, event ticket, store card, generic) where style determines layout and the relevance window (airport arrival versus movie time), distribution channels with the Add to Wallet badge (auto-localized), certificate signing with lifecycle consequences (expired certificates keep installed passes working but block updates; revoked kills them), and iCloud multi-device sync.
records.traversal: Concept sections to PassKit documentation; HIG linked for design best practices.
records.responsiveBehavior: Guide sections stack; badge artwork scales responsively.
records.visualWorld: Commerce-adjacent docs where certificate lifecycle consequences are spelled out as operational rules.
strengths: Pass style is taught as a behavior choice (relevance window), not just a visual one
Certificate expiry versus revocation consequences are distinguished precisely
The Add to Wallet badge is auto-localized via the API, removing asset-management work
weaknesses: Pass design detail defers to the HIG, splitting the guidance across two sites
No visual gallery of the five styles on this page
transferableDecisions: Teach object styles as behavior choices with different relevance rules
Document credential lifecycle consequences (expiry versus revocation) explicitly

records.responsiveBehavior: Code blocks scroll horizontally; nav collapses to a drawer.
records.visualWorld: Design-platform developer docs where security defaults (PKCE mandatory) pair with in-portal tooling that removes URL-building errors.
strengths: PKCE is not optional, removing a whole class of insecure implementations

weaknesses: Prerequisites push real work into the Developer Portal before the guide becomes actionable
Scopes are an appendix hop away from the authorization URL section that needs them
transferableDecisions: Mandate PKCE instead of offering weaker flows
Build parameter pre-fill tooling into the developer portal, leaving secrets to the developer

records.title: Discord OAuth2 Documentation

weaknesses: Scope table length buries the commonly used scopes among partner-only ones
No quickstart beside the reference for first-time OAuth implementers
transferableDecisions: Print transport contracts (content type requirements) next to endpoint URLs
Mark gated capabilities with their escalation path inline

records.title: Linear homepage
records.firstScreenJob: Frame the product as a full system, then prove it by dropping the visitor directly into a detailed product simulation.
records.topology: A minimal top nav and CTA rail sits above a long homepage built from one immersive hero simulation followed by numbered product-story chapters for intake, planning, building, review, and monitoring.
records.traversal: Traversal is strongly sequential: hero proof first, then a numbered scroll story with chapter links like 1.0 Intake through 5.0 Monitor that progressively widen the product scope.
records.responsiveBehavior: The fetched page is presented as a single-column narrative with nav, hero simulation, and stacked chapter sections; exact breakpoint swaps or mobile-only controls were not directly observable.
records.motion: The text capture exposed static image placeholders and no inspectable timing data; any animation in the live product frames was not directly observable here.
records.visualWorld: Editorial software showcase with dense in-product snapshots, numbered chaptering, restrained chrome, and a strong sense of operational realism built from issue text, agents, diffs, and dashboards.
strengths: The hero demonstrates the product in context instead of opening with abstract brand copy.
Numbered chapter structure gives the long page a memorable narrative spine.
The simulated data is specific enough to make the product feel operational rather than conceptual.
weaknesses: The first screen is cognitively heavy and may overwhelm visitors who do not already understand the category.
Headline repetition in the fetched output weakens crispness at the top of the page.
The homepage commits hard to one dense product-story mode rather than offering a lighter skim path early.
transferableDecisions: Use one believable scenario with domain-specific data to establish credibility immediately.
Organize long homepages as explicit chapters when the product spans multiple jobs.
Let proof modules show artifacts, actor names, and state changes instead of relying on generic feature cards.

records.title: SF Symbols Library
records.firstScreenJob: Present a 7,000-plus symbol library whose symbols align with the system font, animate in layers, and localize across 20 scripts.
records.topology: Product page for the symbol system: scale claims (7,000+ symbols, nine weights, three scales, automatic text alignment), Enhanced Search with semantic understanding, new symbols for iOS 27, then the animation system in depth: Draw On and Draw Off presets with annotation guide points that translate across weights, playback modes (whole symbol, by layer, individually), Variable Rendering for progress indication, choreography presets (Bounce, Wiggle, Rotate, Breathe), Magic Replace transitions, and four rendering modes (Monochrome, Hierarchical, Palette).
records.traversal: Feature sections linearly; download and gallery links for the companion app.
records.responsiveBehavior: Sections stack; symbol visuals scale to viewport.
records.visualWorld: Icon-system documentation where animation choreography is specified as precisely as the glyphs themselves.
strengths: Animation presets are documented with layer-level mechanics (guide points, per-layer offsets), not just named
Localization is structural: symbols adapt to reading direction with localized designs for over 20 scripts
Variable Rendering turns icons into progress indicators, extending the symbol semantic range
weaknesses: Version-gated symbols (iOS 27) complicate adoption decisions for older targets
Animation options are numerous enough to invite inconsistency without app-level rules
transferableDecisions: Document icon animation at the layer-mechanics level
Build localization (reading direction, script variants) into the asset system itself

records.title: StoreKit 2 In-App Purchase
records.firstScreenJob: Sell StoreKit 2 as Swift-first commerce with one-line merchandising views and cryptographically signed transactions.
records.topology: Feature page: Swift-first APIs (Swift concurrency, entitlement and offer-eligibility checks, transaction history parity with the App Store Server API), three merchandising views (StoreView, ProductView, SubscriptionStoreView) that present description, price, and duration with as little as one line of code plus built-in localization, security via JSON Web Signature signed transactions with automatic cross-device availability, customer support APIs (in-app refund requests, subscription management, renewal-date extension), and sandbox testing in Xcode.
records.traversal: Feature sections to documentation; localized documentation links (Chinese, Japanese) in resources.
records.responsiveBehavior: Sections stack on mobile.
records.visualWorld: Commerce-platform docs where merchandising UI ships as framework views, collapsing design and implementation into one API call.
strengths: Merchandising views reduce a purchase screen to one line of code with localization included
Transaction parity between client and server APIs prevents reconciliation drift
Signed transactions (JWS) make verification a parsing task instead of a server round-trip design
weaknesses: One-line views trade customizability for speed, with customization depth left undocumented here
Refund flows depend on Apple-side decisions outside developer control
transferableDecisions: Ship merchandising UI as framework views with localization built in
Keep client and server transaction APIs information-identical

records.title: Twitch Authentication Guide

records.traversal: Concept to per-flow detail pages; a contents box mirrors the section order.
records.responsiveBehavior: Decision tables reflow to stacked rows on mobile.
records.visualWorld: Streaming-platform auth docs that decide for you: each flow names the exact application architecture it serves.
strengths: Flow choice is mapped to concrete app types (set-top boxes, games, Electron) instead of abstract criteria
The EventSub app-token exception is called out before it can cause a failing integration

weaknesses: Two token types plus six flow variants is a dense first read for newcomers
The permission dialog example is described in prose rather than shown
transferableDecisions: Map auth flows to concrete application architectures
Document token-type exceptions (webhooks needing app tokens) before the matrix

records.title: Wear OS Tiles
records.firstScreenJob: Teach tiles as glance-only surfaces with hard constraints: no scrolling, small information dose, no long-running work.
records.topology: Developer guide: tile interaction model (carousel revealed by swiping the watch face, tiles cannot scroll, users choose their tiles), the declarative protolayout model rendered in a separate remote environment (different load, display, and update approaches), then core principles as rules: do not overcrowd (tap through to the app for more), the system owns final rendering, and no frequent fetching or long-running async work in the tile service (use WorkManager and cache results).
records.traversal: Concept to core principles to migration notes (ProtoLayout namespaces).
records.responsiveBehavior: Single-column guide with figure.
records.visualWorld: Constraint-driven design documentation where the rendering architecture (remote environment) justifies the content rules.
strengths: The glance constraint is stated as seconds of attention, setting a concrete content budget
Performance rules name the mechanism (WorkManager, local cache), not just the prohibition
System-owns-rendering is stated up front, preventing pixel-control assumptions
weaknesses: No visual gallery of well-designed versus overcrowded tiles
Update-frequency guidance lacks concrete numbers
transferableDecisions: State attention budgets (glance seconds) as design constraints
Pair every performance prohibition with the sanctioned mechanism
records.rightsNote: Text notes and canonical link only; page extract cached locally, not committed.

records.title: YouTube Live Streaming
records.firstScreenJob: Gate live streaming behind explicit requirements, then route to one of four streaming methods by use case.
records.topology: Creator support article: enable requirements as a gating list (16 or older, verified channel, no live restrictions in the past 90 days, chat limits for streams featuring 13-15 year olds without an accompanying adult), then Choose a way to stream - Mobile tagged good for vlogging and quick updates, Webcam for quick computer streams, Encoder for gameplay, overlays, and hardware at gaming events, sports, concerts, and conferences, plus game consoles; format strategy follows with vertical streams getting a full-screen Shorts-feed experience with fan funding (Super Chat, Super Stickers, memberships, gifts) and dual horizontal-plus-vertical streaming via a Live Control Room toggle; engagement features (pin messages, live polls, Q and A, reactions) close the page.
records.traversal: Requirements, method picker, format options, engagement features; related-article rail at the foot.
records.responsiveBehavior: Single-column steps; method sections collapse into stacked blocks on mobile.
records.visualWorld: Google creator-help skin where each streaming method carries an explicit best-use tag.
strengths: Every streaming method is tagged with its best use case (mobile for vlogging, encoder for gameplay and events)
Gating requirements state consequences, not just rules (takedown, temporary loss of live access)
Vertical and dual-format streaming framed as a discovery surface through the Shorts feed
weaknesses: Enablement, methods, and engagement features mixed into one long page without a summary
Availability caveats (third-party encoder not yet supported for dual stream) buried mid-procedure
transferableDecisions: Attach a good-for use case to every method choice
State gating requirements together with their consequences

records.topology: Product page inside a platform narrative: mega-nav spans Meetings, Chat, Phone, Mail, Calendar, Scheduler, Whiteboard, Clips, plus Zoom CX, Zoom AI (ZoomMate, My Notes, Virtual Agent, AI On-Prem), and Developers (Video SDK, Co-Browse, marketplace, MCP Realtime Media Streams); page H2s are outcome phrases - Drive impact with AI, Improve meeting outcomes, Work from anywhere, Video conferencing built for modern work, Streamline meeting workflows, Reduce silos increase productivity, Collaborate across hybrid teams, Move work forward with ZoomMate by your side.
records.traversal: Mega-nav, outcome sections, app-store badges, and contact-sales CTAs throughout.
records.responsiveBehavior: Mega-nav collapses into a hamburger with grouped panels on mobile.
records.visualWorld: Enterprise SaaS product page where every section header is an outcome claim.
strengths: The single product is sold inside the platform story (Zoom Workplace, AI-first) rather than standalone
Section headers are outcome phrases (Improve meeting outcomes, Reduce silos) instead of feature names
The developer ecosystem (Video SDK, marketplace) is first-class navigation, not a footer link
weaknesses: The mega-nav carries dozens of product entries, risking choice paralysis
AI branding repeats across overlapping nav sections (Zoom AI, AI at Zoom, AI Resources) with unclear boundaries
transferableDecisions: Sell the individual product inside the platform narrative
Phrase section headers as user outcomes
records.rightsNote: Text notes and canonical link only; page extract cached locally, not committed.

records.title: Zoom OAuth 2.0 Integration Guide
records.firstScreenJob: Organize OAuth by app type (Server-to-Server versus General) with complete request and response examples.
records.topology: Integration guide keyed by authorization use case: Server-to-Server uses account_credentials with the account ID and no separate refresh flow (request a new token after the one-hour expiry), General uses the user authorization code flow with Local Test page installation; every step shows full HTTP examples including the Base64 basic-auth header, JSON responses with expires_in and scope, plus deauthorization and PKCE sections.
records.traversal: Use-case sections via on-page outline (request, refresh, revoke, use, me context, deauthorization, PKCE).
records.responsiveBehavior: HTTP examples scroll horizontally; outline collapses on mobile.
records.visualWorld: Meeting-platform docs where token lifecycle rules (one-hour expiry, no refresh flow for server apps) are stated as plainly as the happy path.
strengths: Complete request and response pairs are shown, including header construction
The no-refresh-flow rule for server-to-server is stated explicitly, preventing a common wrong assumption
Re-authorization triggers (scope or webhook changes) are documented where the authorization flow is taught
weaknesses: App-type taxonomy (Server-to-Server, General) assumes marketplace knowledge
Rivet library note adds a parallel abstraction without explaining when to prefer it
transferableDecisions: Key OAuth docs by app type with complete request-response pairs
State token-expiry and refresh rules (or their absence) explicitly
records.rightsNote: Text notes and canonical link only; page extract cached locally, not committed.

patterns.name: Card grid for heterogeneous telemetry
patterns.problem: An authenticated home must show many unlike signals (metrics, tips, announcements, tasks) without collapsing them into one monolithic chart or endless list.
worksWhen: Signals differ in type and update cadence, so each card can own one job
Users return frequently and scan rather than read
Cards can be collapsed, reordered, or gated by eligibility instead of shown as empty shells
failsWhen: Every card gets equal visual weight so nothing reads as primary
Cards multiply without curation and push key signals below the fold
The surface is a focused operator console where one dense table would serve better

patterns.name: Chaptered scroll story for long homepages
patterns.problem: Broad platforms need long homepages, but an undifferentiated scroll of feature cards loses visitors midway.
worksWhen: The page divides into a small set of named narrative chapters
Repeated CTA returns follow each major proof section
Format or audience switches act as visible waypoints
failsWhen: Chapters multiply until the page becomes a sitemap
Each chapter repeats the same layout so waypoints stop registering
A focused single-product page would answer the visitor faster

patterns.name: Create and open existing as equal entries
patterns.problem: Launcher empty and first-run surfaces bury open-existing under create, even when many users already have content elsewhere.
worksWhen: Create new and open existing are equally prominent
Import or attach existing paths are not nested under a single create button
failsWhen: Open existing is hidden behind create or overflow
Users with existing work are forced through a blank create funnel

patterns.name: Density toggle for high-volume libraries
patterns.problem: Media and content libraries lock users into one density even when collections range from dozens to tens of thousands of items.
worksWhen: Users can switch density without leaving the library surface
Default grouping still uses a natural temporal or categorical dimension
failsWhen: High-volume collections only offer one cramped or one sparse view
Density changes reset filters or scroll position unexpectedly

patterns.name: Keep destructive actions in overflow
patterns.problem: Library and setup surfaces place delete, reset, or overwrite actions next to the primary create CTA, increasing mis-taps.
worksWhen: Destructive actions sit in a secondary overflow away from the primary CTA
Import and export remain first-class but still separated from delete
failsWhen: Delete and create share the same visual weight
Destructive actions appear as unlabeled icons near the main action

patterns.name: Editable KPI canvas for expert homes
patterns.problem: Expert operators have divergent priorities, so a fixed KPI home either overwhelms some users or starves others.
worksWhen: Users are experts who know which metrics matter to them
Tile units, movement, and resizing are documented first-class behaviors
Scope and time controls stay persistent in the top bar
failsWhen: Casual users face a blank or misconfigured canvas
Personal customization fragments shared team awareness
Permission gates leave most operators unable to edit what they see

patterns.name: Empty-state outcome headline with one CTA
patterns.problem: Empty library and launcher surfaces either offer no action or overwhelm users with multiple competing CTAs.
worksWhen: The empty state has a clear outcome headline and one primary action
The surface is a first-visit or depleted library rather than an error panel
failsWhen: Multiple CTAs compete for attention on the empty canvas
The headline describes absence instead of the outcome the user will achieve

patterns.name: Essential versus advanced option tiers
patterns.problem: Library and setup forms expose every option at equal weight, delaying the first successful configuration.
worksWhen: Essential options are visible by default and advanced options stay collapsed
Type or mode selection determines which advanced options appear
failsWhen: Experts and novices face the same dense option wall
Advanced options appear before the user has chosen a type or mode

patterns.name: Job verbs over abstract slogans
patterns.problem: Public homepages for tools drift into abstract benefit language that fails to tell visitors what they can actually do.
worksWhen: Capabilities are named with the user's own working verbs
The hero states one end-to-end workflow promise before feature detail
Advanced power is expressed through a few memorable verbs instead of a matrix
failsWhen: The audience buys on brand feeling rather than capability
Verb lists grow so long they become the matrix they replaced
Enterprise buyers need proof and compliance language more than verbs

patterns.name: Just-in-time permission requests
patterns.problem: Mobile and creation onboarding ask for permissions before the user understands why, increasing denial rates.
worksWhen: The permission prompt appears at the moment the capability is needed
The preceding UI explains the value of granting access in concrete terms
failsWhen: Permissions are stacked into an early onboarding checklist
The product asks for access without linking it to an immediate action

patterns.name: Choose library type before path
patterns.problem: Library setup asks for folder paths before the user commits to a content type, which forces rework when the type changes options.
worksWhen: Type selection comes first and orients subsequent path and scanner options
Advanced options stay collapsed until the type is chosen
failsWhen: Path entry precedes type and makes type-dependent options feel arbitrary
All library options appear at equal weight regardless of type

patterns.name: Mobile home as summary, not console
patterns.problem: Porting a full operator console to mobile produces cramped controls, so mobile homes must choose a narrower job.
worksWhen: The mobile surface is an at-a-glance summary with deep links to focused screens
Bottom tabs carry primary destinations and one launcher covers quick actions
Owners prepare a phone view instead of letting desktop layouts reflow
failsWhen: Creation or configuration tasks are forced into the mobile shell
Uniform portrait stacking flattens hierarchy without a prepared phone layout
The summary hides so much that operators must always switch to desktop

patterns.name: Persist library filters across sessions
patterns.problem: High-frequency library filters reset every visit, forcing repeated taps on mobile and dense launchers.
worksWhen: Filter and sort selection survive session boundaries
The default filter still remains easy to clear or override
failsWhen: Users must reselect the same filter every return visit
Persisted filters hide important new content without a reset path

patterns.name: Pinned shortcuts above the main list
patterns.problem: Dense libraries bury the few highest-frequency destinations inside the same scroll as everything else.
worksWhen: A pinned or shortcut tier sits above the main list for frequent destinations
The main list remains complete and searchable underneath
failsWhen: Every item competes at the same hierarchy level
Pinned rows become another unmanaged favorites dump

patterns.name: Primary table with side diagnostics
patterns.problem: Operators need object-level work (rows) and account-level awareness (quotas, compliance, status) at the same time without switching pages.
worksWhen: A content or order table is the main workspace and side panels carry persistent constraints
Compliance or quota indicators must stay visible while acting on rows
Filters live above the table instead of hidden in advanced search
failsWhen: Side panels grow into a second competing workspace
The account signals update rarely enough that a settings page suffices
Small viewports force the panels to stack and bury the table

patterns.name: Resume-in-progress leads the home
patterns.problem: Returning users of creation or consumption tools want to continue prior work, but many homes lead with discovery or marketing modules instead.
worksWhen: Return visits dominate over first visits
Recent objects are unambiguous and safe to surface
A recents lane can sit beside starred or favorited lanes for different return jobs
failsWhen: The product is session-less so recency has no meaning
Recents expose sensitive content on shared screens
New-user onboarding needs the first screen more than continuation does

patterns.name: Safety controls one layer deep
patterns.problem: Hosts and moderators need intervention controls during live events, but burying them in settings makes response too slow while inlining all of them crowds the surface.
worksWhen: A dedicated panel or menu groups all safety actions one tap from the main view
Roles (host, co-host, moderator) have documented capability differences
High-frequency actions (block, slow mode, mute) are closest to the content they act on
failsWhen: Critical safety rules hide behind multiple navigation layers
The toolbar accumulates every feature until scanning fails under pressure
Role differences are so intricate that operators misremember who can act

patterns.name: Saved views over repeated search
patterns.problem: Operators repeat the same filtered queries daily; making them re-derive filters wastes time and invites inconsistency.
worksWhen: Filter combinations recur and deserve named, persistent views
Views appear as a visible strip or list, not buried in menus
Sorting, grouping, and column choices persist per view
failsWhen: View proliferation makes the tab strip itself unscannable
No governance exists so team views drift into private dialects
The dataset is small enough that one default view suffices

patterns.name: Persistent non-modal scan progress
patterns.problem: Long-running library scans or imports either block navigation with modal progress or hide status so users cannot tell whether work continues.
worksWhen: Scan or import work can continue while the user browses other areas
Progress is visible but non-blocking on the library surface
failsWhen: Progress is shown only in a modal that freezes navigation
Status disappears after start with no persistent indicator

patterns.name: Stable shell as orientation layer
patterns.problem: Dense authenticated products disorient users when navigation chrome shifts with content, especially across many destinations.
worksWhen: A persistent header and side nav stay fixed while only the content region changes
Side-nav groups expand for products that outgrow flat header navigation
Focus return and collapse behavior are specified, not left to chance
failsWhen: The shell consumes so much space that content starves on laptops
Every module invents its own shell variant and orientation breaks
A single-surface tool gains bureaucracy from a shell it does not need

patterns.name: Suite homepage as routing layer
patterns.problem: Multi-product suites overload a single persuasion page; visitors with different intents need different destinations fast.
worksWhen: The homepage treats itself as a discovery map with one sharp line per product
Roles, use cases, or team entry points widen relevance without duplicating pages
Platform, solution, and learning routes stay separated in navigation
failsWhen: Routing tiles replace any actual persuasion so the page feels like a directory
A single flagship product deserves the hero instead of the suite
Visitors cannot tell products apart from one-line descriptions

patterns.name: Wizard only for dependent steps
patterns.problem: Creation flows become wizards by default even when steps are independent, adding friction without dependency payoff.
worksWhen: Later steps require confirmation or data from earlier ones
The flow shows step count and allows back navigation except for irreversible commits
failsWhen: All settings could be completed safely on one form
Back navigation discards prior input or steps feel irreversible without reason

patterns.name: Working canvas as hero proof
patterns.problem: Builder products claim control and power, but generic mockups leave the claim unproven on the first screen.
worksWhen: The hero shows the real working canvas with navigation, layers, and publish actions visible
Realistic interface chrome carries the proof instead of abstract illustration
One believable scenario with domain-specific data anchors credibility
failsWhen: The product UI is too dense to read at hero scale
A staged screenshot drifts from the shipped product and erodes trust
The audience is non-technical and reads the canvas as complexity

patterns.name: Workspace picker before naming
patterns.problem: Creation forms ask for names and details before the user chooses the permission or workspace context those details belong to.
worksWhen: Workspace or destination picker is the first consequential step
Naming and templates appear only after permission context is clear
failsWhen: Users name an object and then discover they created it in the wrong workspace
Permission context is buried below advanced settings
